# Google Play Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/google-play-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/google-play-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects app data from play.google.com (Google Play Store), written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape Google Play App Reviews and Data](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-google-play-app-reviews-and-data)
- **Code:** [`google_play.py`](google_play.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [App](results/app.json) · [Reviews](results/reviews.json) · [Search](results/search.json)

## What it scrapes

- Google Play app detail pages for app data
- Google Play app reviews
- Google Play search pages for app listing data

## Functions

- `scrape_apps(app_ids, lang='en', country='us')` → `List[Dict]`: scrape Google Play app detail pages
- `scrape_reviews(app_id, lang='en', country='us', sort=Sort.NEWEST, max_reviews=100, filter_score_with=None)` → `List[Dict]`: scrape app reviews via the Play Store batchexecute endpoint
- `scrape_search(query, lang='en', country='us')` → `List[Dict]`: scrape Google Play search results

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import google_play


async def main():
    apps = await google_play.scrape_apps(app_ids=["com.whatsapp", "com.spotify.music"])
    reviews = await google_play.scrape_reviews(app_id="com.whatsapp", max_reviews=100)
    search = await google_play.scrape_search(query="Music")


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields of the sample output (top-level keys of the first item):

- [`results/app.json`](results/app.json): `title`, `description`, `descriptionHTML`, `summary`, `installs`, `minInstalls`, `realInstalls`, `score`, `ratings`, `reviews`, `histogram`, `price`, `free`, `currency`, `offersIAP`, `inAppProductPrice`, `developer`, `developerId`, `developerEmail`, `developerWebsite`, `developerAddress`, `privacyPolicy`, `genre`, `genreId`, `categories`, `icon`, `headerImage`, `screenshots`, `video`, `videoImage`, `contentRating`, `contentRatingDescription`, `adSupported`, `containsAds`, `released`, `lastUpdatedOn`, `updated`, `version`, `comments`, `appId`, … (1 more)
- [`results/reviews.json`](results/reviews.json): `reviewId`, `userName`, `userImage`, `content`, `score`, `thumbsUpCount`, `reviewCreatedVersion`, `at`, `replyContent`, `repliedAt`, `appVersion`
- [`results/search.json`](results/search.json): `appId`, `icon`, `screenshots`, `title`, `score`, `genre`, `price`, `free`, `currency`, `video`, `videoImage`, `description`, `descriptionHTML`, `developer`, `installs`

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`google_play.py`](google_play.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `asp` = `True`: Anti Scraping Protection, the earlier name of the [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker)
- `country` = `"US"`: country of the proxy

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/google-play-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_app_scraping`, `test_reviews_scraping`, `test_search_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
